Timestamp labels below come from that recovered transcript. Do not infer the exact minute of a sub-event unless it is supplied. ### 7:35 AM — Gloin follows Borin to the Copper Anvil - The player initially selected the Royal Army enlistment opportunity with the explicit qualification that Gloin wished to question Borin about the mine first. This established an intention to investigate military service, not an actual enlistment, signing of a contract, or trip to the recruitment office. - Gloin followed Borin from the Lower Eastern Quarter noticeboard and found him about ten minutes later outside a small alehouse called the Copper Anvil, sitting on a wooden bench and drinking dark ale. - Borin greeted him: “Thought you'd be following me.” He said the sealed mine had once produced excellent iron in the western Ironspines. The publicly accepted explanation for closure 63 years earlier was collapse of the lower galleries, but Borin challenged this story. - Borin's account, not independently verified at this point: miners found something other than iron: a chamber under the oldest workings. Royal surveyors sealed it; those who had seen it were ordered not to discuss it. Borin was an apprentice engineer and helped seal the lower access, but specifically said he had not been inside the chamber. - Borin said three engineers who would not cooperate disappeared. He explained his years of silence by recalling that he had a wife and two young daughters. This establishes what he said of his circumstances then, not the present status or ages of his family. - A Royal Mining Office visitor had come looking for him roughly a month earlier, asking after the original survey. Borin had denied possessing one and now admitted to Gloin, “That was a lie.” - Borin said the survey was hidden at his home and he would not simply hand it over. He discussed the possibility of Gloin joining the Royal Army: ordinary recruits would serve an initial three-year term, train as infantry, receive crown-supplied equipment, pay, meals and barracks lodging; advancement was possible. The Crownward recruitment office was said to be roughly a twenty-minute journey away. Borin cautioned that a uniform did not guarantee safety and that the king's servants did not always tell the king everything. This is Borin's warning, not proof of wrongdoing. ### 7:50–8:05 AM — Borin's home and three surviving survey sheets - When asked for his next decision at 7:50 AM, the player explicitly chose to ask Borin to show the survey and, at his house after examining it, ask about the engineers and the visitor. - By the story's 8:05 AM heading, Borin had brought Gloin into an older residential district of the Eastern Quarter, where the buildings were dark granite with iron-reinforced doors. His modest, maintained house had a lit stone fireplace, old mining tools above the hearth and framed family portraits. - Borin moved a heavy cabinet and unlocked a narrow wooden case holding yellowing survey parchments. He spread three sheets on his dining table. He said his copy was incomplete: he had kept the sections he personally worked on and royal engineers took the rest. - Physical survey observations: the public mine maps depicted six operational levels while Borin's private survey depicted nine; lower galleries were smooth and mathematically laid out, with precisely spaced pillars unlike normal mining passages. Under the ninth level was a marked chamber translated by Borin as the Hall Beneath the Mountain. The survey did not depict a conventional chamber entrance; a narrow passage ended at a sealed stone doorway. - A marginal note on the survey said: “Sound observed beyond the western wall. No machinery identified.” It was dated three days before the official sealing 63 years earlier. This is documentary evidence of a historical report, not proof of the sound's cause. - Engineers named by Borin: Thrain Coppervein, chief surveyor responsible for the lower measurements, vanished first; Orik Feldspar, structural engineer overseeing the sealing work, disappeared six weeks later; Dorin Blackmantle, royal inspector conducting the official investigation, was last seen going into the Crownward district. Borin said none returned to their families, no bodies or funerals were known, and there had been no official compensation. Borin personally knew Orik and said Orik had three children. He could not establish whether the engineers were murdered. - Visitor description from Borin: He had come 27 days before this conversation, looked perhaps 60 years old, had a neatly trimmed black beard, a scar running from the right ear toward the jaw, a silver royal mining signet, and an educated northern accent. Borin thought him unusually young for the office he claimed. He had asked specifically whether the old survey mentioned the Hall Beneath the Mountain. - The visitor allegedly said that noises had returned in the lower galleries: three knocks behind the sealed doorway, as reported by night watchmen. Borin had not heard the knocks himself; at this stage this was second-hand testimony. ### The interruption and Gloin's decision to hide rather than escape - The conversation was interrupted by repeated groups of three sharp knocks at Borin's front door, followed by a voice identifying the Royal Mining Office. Borin believed this was the same visitor or his associate, and mentioned a workshop rear exit. - The player clarified the intended action as “Instead of escape hide and eavesdrop”. Although a following generated action-card label also referred to “use the rear entrance,” the narrated action unmistakably shows Gloin staying and listening. Do not record a workshop escape or departure here. - Borin returned the survey parchments to their case and hid the case beneath a loose floorboard near the workshop. Gloin concealed himself in a narrow alcove behind stacked iron barrels. Borin returned to the main room and admitted the visitors. The original survey remained with Borin. ### 8:44 AM — Edrik Voss and the royal guard (Gloin's firsthand eavesdropping) - The visitor was the dwarf matching Borin's description: dark-blue travel coat, neatly trimmed beard, scar from right ear toward jaw, silver signet at his belt. A larger dwarf accompanied him in dark royal-guard leather armour, keeping a hand near his sword. No name for the guard is supplied. - The man identified himself as Edrik Voss, Deputy Examiner of the Royal Mining Office. He said the Crown had authorised renewed inspection of the old eastern mine and that his office sought surviving private surveys. He specifically requested Borin's ninth-level survey. - Edrik alluded to unusual measurements made by Thrain Coppervein. Borin said, “Thrain is dead.” Edrik responded, “Is he?” and asserted that there was no official record of Thrain's death. This exchange does not confirm Thrain is alive, nor does it establish his cause of death. - Borin denied having any records. Edrik accused him of lying. The guard's presence and Edrik's remarks made the meeting intimidating; the transcript records no physical assault. - Edrik's unverified account: the western wall was breached eleven nights earlier. Asked what was found, he said “Nothing,” then claimed “Because something came through.” He said night watch heard three knocks followed by unfamiliar voices, but gave no independently verified identity, description or evidence of anything passing through. - Edrik said the Crown wanted the matter contained and that His Majesty had not been informed of the breach. He said the investigation was under Lord Chancellor Veyron's authority. This is Edrik's statement, not verified knowledge about what King Durgan IV knew or Veyron's motives. - Edrik warned he would return in two days and urged Borin to produce the survey; this was a threatened return, not a recorded future visit. He also warned Borin against speaking of the matter and briefly looked toward the workshop. The look alone does not prove he saw Gloin, knew Gloin's identity, or discovered the hiding place. - Edrik and the guard left. Gloin then emerged unharmed. Gloin had personally heard Edrik say these things, but had not witnessed a western-wall breach, heard the reported mine knocks himself, or seen an entity. ### By 9:06 AM — Hammer-and-Crown seal and Hadrik lead - Borin retrieved his survey case from the floorboard. He said the old lower galleries had been constructed by dwarves but not for ordinary mining; this is his interpretation grounded in the architecture. - Borin pointed to a survey mark near the western wall resembling a hammer crossed with a crown. He characterised it as an older royal seal, predating the Stonehand dynasty. - Borin identified Master Scholar Hadrik Ironvein of the Royal Historical Archive as someone likely able to understand the mark. Gloin had not yet met Hadrik. - At 9:06 AM, Borin and Gloin were still in Borin's home. Borin offered drinks; the Royal Army recruitment option remained unpursued and Gloin was still unemployed, healthy and not enlisted. His purse remained 18 silver crowns, with no recorded purchase in these excerpts. ### 9:12 AM — The First Throne and a scholar's introduction - The player selected the action to ask Borin to explain the old royal seal, then introduce Gloin to Hadrik. - Borin took a worn leather-covered book from his shelf and showed Gloin the same symbol. He named it the Hammer and Crown, seal of the First Throne, a purported older Khazari sovereignty predating the Seven Mountain Thrones and the Stonehand dynasty. - Borin associated the First Throne with Thargrim the Deepfather, legendary founder who united original mountain clans and established laws for the deep halls. He guessed the legacy was at least 3,000 years old, perhaps older. Do not confuse this legendary founder with Thargrim IV, the later last universally acknowledged sovereign described elsewhere in the historical canon. - Borin said the First Throne was abandoned rather than conquered. He presented conflicting explanations: the Deepfather may have died; others claimed he sealed something beneath the mountain and ordered departure. An illustration of an immense stone doorway bearing the Hammer and Crown resembled the architecture shown in the mine survey. Borin and the narration regarded the resemblance as strong, but a common symbol does not independently prove what lies beyond the sealed doorway. - Borin said conventional teaching placed modern Khazari origins in seven mountain clans, while disputed or forbidden texts suggested an advanced First Throne civilisation had existed earlier, employing remarkable engineering and runecraft; some scholars speculated its deep structures were built for an unfinished purpose. These are reported texts and scholarly theories, not confirmation of a hidden project. - Borin described Hadrik as roughly 176, senior researcher at the Royal Historical Archive, politically unpopular because of his inquiries. Borin said Hadrik had been ordered to cease First Throne research as historically unreliable, but had not stopped. Borin and Hadrik were longtime acquaintances. - Borin agreed to introduce Gloin but requested: “Don't mention Edrik Voss until we know whether Hadrik can be trusted.” This is a request; whether Gloin later obeyed it must be determined from subsequent transcript, not presumed. ### By 9:35 AM — First meeting with Hadrik Ironvein - Borin and Gloin travelled into the affluent Crownward district, passing government offices, official traffic, noble carriages, wide streets and monumental stone arches. Two armoured soldiers guarded the Royal Historical Archive's entrance. - They found Hadrik in a private reading chamber among books and papers. Hadrik recognised Borin: “Ashmantle! I thought you were dead.” Borin answered “Not yet.” The two embraced briefly. - Hadrik turned to Gloin and asked, “And who is this?” He welcomed Gloin's interest in scholarship and asked, “Tell me, what brings you to my archive?” - The recovered scene explicitly says that Hadrik had not yet been told about the survey at that instant. Borin remained quiet. At this 9:35 AM arrival Hadrik did not know about the survey, but a newly recovered set of screenshots now documents Gloin's cautious interview with Hadrik starting at 9:38 AM, below. The later Day 22 archive meeting remains the current verified campaign pause. - 9:35 AM ledger: location Royal Historical Archive, health good, purse 18 silver, occupation unemployed, Royal Army not enlisted, Gloin's canonical age 42. Borin still has the original survey. Edrik's assertions and the fate of the missing engineers remain open. ### 9:35–9:38 AM — Gloin tests Hadrik's loyalties before disclosing the mine Source: Ten overlapping original-chat screenshots supplied by the creator, IMG\_2767 through IMG\_2776. These establish the original 9:35 AM character ledger, selected approach and story scene labelled Autumn Day 19, 9:38 AM. The iPhone's 10:33–10:34 display is a device clock, not a campaign timestamp. The last screenshot cuts off before the full response/next decision is visible. 9:35 AM incoming ledger and direct dialogue: Gloin, a healthy Khazari of Karak-Varn, was at the Royal Historical Archive with 18 silver crowns, unemployed, not enlisted and of unknown reputation; his canonical age is 42, superseding the screenshot's obsolete “34” character-table entry. His current knowledge ledger listed the Hammer and Crown as the First Throne seal; the First Throne's antiquity relative to the Seven Thrones; Thargrim the Deepfather's legendary founding association; deliberate First Throne abandonment; resemblance between ancient architecture and the sealed chamber; and possible superiority of old Khazari engineering. Such entries record what Gloin had been told or learned, not proof that every ancient interpretation is correct. Relationships were recorded as Borin a trusted acquaintance, Hadrik newly introduced and academically cautious, and Edrik Voss a suspicious royal official. The open issues were the Hall Beneath the Mountain, the missing engineers, the reported recent breach, Lord Chancellor Veyron, and the First Throne's disappearance. Hadrik folded his hands and asked Gloin: “Well then, young one. What exactly are you interested in?” The player was offered several ways to proceed — discuss the Hammer and Crown, the Hall Beneath the Mountain, Borin's survey, Thargrim and the First Throne, the Crown's prohibition of Hadrik's research, or caution and trust-building. The player selected “Be cautious and establish trust first”, with the exact additional direction “Try and find exactly where his loyalty lies”. The submitted action was “Keep things vague and get to know him first”, explicitly preserving the established story. 9:38 AM, “A scholar's company”: Gloin accepted a chair. Rather than immediately disclose the mine, the generated scene has him explain a general interest in Khazari history, particularly older kingdoms, and ask about Hadrik's work, studies and tenure. Borin remained quietly beside him. Hadrik seemed pleased and said: - “One hundred and twelve years in this institution. Forty of those spent studying periods that the Crown would rather forget.” - “History is an interesting profession. The dead cannot defend themselves, and the living are often too concerned with their reputations to tell the truth.” These are Hadrik's own statements about experience and outlook, not independent proof of wrongdoing by a particular official. “Testing his loyalties”: The narrated dialogue turns to whether Hadrik considered himself loyal to the Crown. He responded: - “I am loyal to Karak-Varn. I am loyal to the Khazari. I am loyal to our people and their history.” - “Kings, however, are temporary. Governments change. Noble houses rise and fall. I have served three kings, and I expect to outlive at least one more.” - When asked if he would oppose a king he believed wrong: “I would hope a good king surrounds himself with dwarves willing to tell him when he is wrong.” - “But I have little patience for those who use royal authority to conceal the truth.” - Asked if that happened often: “More often than the history books suggest.” - Looking toward the upper archive galleries, he added: “Especially when ancient discoveries threaten modern political arrangements.” “The old prohibition”: Gloin then gently asked why Hadrik's own research had been prohibited. Hadrik answered that approximately 40 years earlier, while studying the First Throne, he found contradictions between official histories and older inscriptions. According to Hadrik, royal archivists instructed him to suspend the research by administrative order, with no criminal charges and no trial. Borin gave Hadrik a warning look when he began discussing it, but Hadrik continued. Asked what he found, he said: - “Evidence that the First Throne did not simply disappear. It was dismantled politically, and its surviving institutions were deliberately erased from our historical record.” - “I suspect someone was afraid that a competing claim to legitimate rule might emerge.” Crucial qualification: This is Hadrik's claimed discovery and political interpretation. The original narrator explicitly stated that Hadrik did not claim an actual surviving heir, institution or legitimate rival claimant had been found. Do not make an extant First Throne monarchy, secret heir, conspiracy, deliberate erasure by a named ruler or Gloin's ancestry an established fact. “A question of trust”: Gloin asked where Hadrik's loyalties lay when the Crown's interests and historical truth conflicted. Hadrik said: - “Young dwarf, I have buried friends who asked that very question.” - He acknowledged his personal caution, family, students and a long-established professional position; these are his stated interests, not evidence of his private motives. - “But I will not knowingly help someone endanger our people merely to protect a noble family's reputation.” He then asked Gloin “Tell me something. Why are you asking?”, looked briefly at Borin, and added “Neither of you has come here simply to discuss history.” Borin audibly exhaled. Hadrik continued: - “I don't need the entire story. But if there is something beneath this mountain that threatens Karak-Varn, I would rather know about it before someone decides to bury the evidence.” Trust and knowledge status at the screenshot boundary: The narrator assessed Hadrik as primarily loyal to Khazari people and history, respectful of the monarchy but not uncritically obedient, sceptical of political interference, cautious rather than reckless. Gloin had deliberately not yet disclosed the specifics of Borin's survey, the mine or Edrik Voss in this newly recovered exchange. Preserve the Day 22 archive pause at approximately 11:25 AM, which is a different meeting with Hadrik. ## Autumn Day 19 — Silver Anvil apprenticeship discussion and first material tests, through 3:06 PM Source and coverage: The creator supplied a newly recovered combined text excerpt beginning mid-sentence during a discussion involving Maela Deepforge, Borin Ashmantle, Hadrik Ironvein and Gloin at the Silver Anvil. On concentrating, Gloin felt a subtle vibration travelling from his palm into his forearm, and the rune faintly illuminated. Maela took the iron from him and said “Interesting.” 2. A copper disc with a simple binding inscription. Gloin felt almost nothing. Do not claim every runic material responds to him. 3. A smooth mountain crystal. Gloin reported a subtle sensation similar to the initial iron response. Maela also tested the material herself and observed a noticeably different response; the transcript does not quantify the difference.
